questions.subject: JAVA_PROGRAMMING
questions.learningObjective: choose between a tail shape and a non-tail shape
questions.stem:
A choir wants each note number printed once while descending and again while the frames unwind, so the output must read 3 2 1 1 2 3. Which written shape produces that order?
static void echo(int n) { /* the shape goes here */ }

options.text: A non-tail shape that prints n, recurses on n - 1, then prints n again
A tail shape whose recursive call is the last statement the method executes
options.misconception: believes a final recursive call still resumes work on the way back up

options.text: A tail shape that carries a String accumulator built one frame at a time
options.misconception: believes an accumulator can restore the ascending half of the order

options.text: A non-tail shape that returns n plus echo(n - 1) and prints the result once
options.misconception: believes arithmetic on the return value can re-emit the earlier numbers

questions.explanation: The order 3 2 1 comes from the calls themselves and 1 2 3 can only come from statements that run after a call returns, so the method needs a statement after the recursive call and is therefore non-tail. Running it confirms echo(3) prints 3 2 1 1 2 3. A tail call ends the frame with nothing owed, so options B and C print only 3 2 1 and lose the ascending half, and D merely sums to 6, which carries no order at all.
questions.hint: Ask what the frame still owes after the recursive call returns.

questions.topic: Base case coverage for sentinel data
questions.learningObjective: write a base case that stops on a sentinel instead of a length
questions.stem:
A roster walker reaches the end of a scores array by hitting a sentinel written into the last slot, not by testing the array length. Which guard must its base case use?
static int totalScore(int[] scores, int i) { /* the guard goes here */ return scores[i] + totalScore(scores, i + 1); }

options.text: scores[i] == -1, because the last slot holds the sentinel and no real score is negative
scores[i] == 0, because a zero score is the natural stopping value for a roster
options.misconception: believes a zero entry always marks the end of the data

options.text: i >= scores.length, because the array bound is the only legal place to stop
options.misconception: believes sentinel data must still be stopped by the array length

options.text: scores[i] < 0, because any negative reading ends the walk as well
options.misconception: believes every negative value is the sentinel rather than one chosen one

questions.explanation: A sentinel base case has to test the exact value the writer agreed to reserve, and -1 cannot be a real score, so scores[i] == -1 is the only safe guard; running it on {5, 7, -1} from index 0 returns 12. Testing == 0 would stop on a genuine zero score, testing < 0 would swallow any negative score, and option C walks straight into the sentinel slot and adds -1 to the total.
questions.hint: The guard has to name the one value the format reserves.
